reading.body:
Profit Finder Pro Software is not a data center, and its zero megawatts should not be counted in any tally of Arizona AI infrastructure.

The listing is a customer relationship management and sales-tracking product sold to small businesses in roofing, solar, contracting, and insurance. Its address in the Scottsdale area of Maricopa County is currently occupied by a different company, TraVek Inc, and the stored coordinates resolve to that occupant rather than to the software business. Nothing publicly available ties either the company or the address to server infrastructure, colocation space, or dedicated data center equipment. The entry originates as a mistagged OpenStreetMap point labeled telecom=data_center.

This matters because capacity assessments are only as good as the facility lists behind them. Arizona's published figures cover four facilities totaling 512 MW, and a phantom entry with no published specifications adds nothing to that number while distorting any count that treats every mapped point as a real site. The mistagging is scattered rather than clustered, with the other rows in the same batch sitting miles away across the Phoenix metro, so no single shared building explains them.

It does not tell the reader anything about actual data center capacity, power demand, or grid conditions in Arizona. It also does not establish how common mistagging is, since the evidence is one point among a batch of eight. With no specifications published, there is no partial figure to correct, only an entry to exclude.
